scope: Separate native attribution from runtime lane; not this sitting's fastest-JVM artifact, and no cross-run time comparison
observation:
B-k M6 observation ledger (observation only; no collector mechanism selected). Source/profile inputs: instrumented counters from checkpoint 2d951ed18; clean no-diagnostics binaries built from pre-instrumentation parent 0a585a5205bb474e5f9087964c6dd5af0c19d7d9. Six baseline profiles are under ~/.cache/nts-scratch/runtime-content-m6/{cyclic-churn,release-acyclic,tree-teardown}.{nts,ntsllvm}.baseline.profile.txt; perf.data and exact stdout/stderr are alongside. They use perf record -e cpu_core/cycles/u on CPU4 inside with-lock. Quiet-core admission passed; the profile wrapper ran 14:41:54–14:43:36 EEST. A system one-minute load value was not retained, so I make no whole-machine-quiet claim. Earlier stats-off profiles of the instrumented binary are excluded because diagnostic hooks still sampled.
Counters (all complete; per-collection mean; C 760 records, LLVM 764):
- C: candidates seen 10,001.26; age buckets [9,999.34, 1.92, 0, 0, 0, 0]; nodes 30,478.79; edges 30,477.83; bytes visited 1,462,981.77; bytes reclaimed 487,583.75; prior-live node revisits 0; traversal/destruction/freeing 472.8/11.7/108.6 us.
- LLVM: candidates seen 10,001.26; same age buckets; nodes 30,478.79; edges 30,477.83; bytes visited 1,462,981.82; bytes reclaimed 487,583.75; prior-live revisits 0; traversal/destruction/freeing 459.9/11.8/104.8 us.
Thus about one third of visited bytes are reclaimed and two thirds remain live; all roots are young. Stats instrumentation made cyclic-churn about 3.2x slower (roughly 109 us stats-off vs 347–357 us stats-on), so phase times are instrumented and not a clean performance attribution. release-acyclic and tree-teardown have no collection records.
Uninstrumented flat profiles, top shares:
- cyclic-churn C / LLVM: nts_collect_pass 45.82% / 43.05%; work 17.49% / 17.52%; nts_each_reference 11.98% / 15.39%; nts_alloc 6.96% / 6.98%; counted release 6.81% / 6.45%.
- release-acyclic C / LLVM: nts_destroy 39.79% / 40.43%; work 26.28% / 26.87%; nts_alloc 15.97% / 14.32%; counted release 10.83% / 11.88%; typed field release 4.05% / 2.96%. No collector invocation. Main's corrected ratios remain 1.58x node / 1.88x Bun AOT.
- tree-teardown C / LLVM: build__region 46.24% / 45.81%; nts_alloc 25.05% / 26.69%; sum 27.77% / 26.22%. No collection; this sitting's bench table reports 0.55x node and 0.21x C++ (control, not a loss).
Plan mapping:
1) cyclic-churn: B-k's adaptive trigger is conditional on repeated visits dominating; measured prior-live repeats are zero, so that branch is not supported. nts regions --rc --no-acquire on this row reports 0 candidates/0 sites, with 41 allocation/storage candidates all Unknown(not analysed). Source keeps 64 parent/child cycles in a ring; each survives at least 64 loop iterations, then replacement detaches an old cycle. Reset-per-iteration is therefore not safe. Planned stage 3 per-site regions may cover a proved cohort, but current analysis proves none, and nothing planned directly targets the measured fresh-young scan/live-byte ratio. This is a plan gap to record before deciding a mechanism.
2) release-acyclic: stage 1 release-by-type has landed and the profile shows only 3–4% typed field-release share remaining; typed collector visitors (next stage-1 item) do not apply because this row never collects. Dominant per-object destruction/free work is explicitly assigned to stage 3 per-site regions in memory.md; there is no collector fix to choose for this row now.
3) tree-teardown is a non-collector control: construction, allocation and checksum dominate; no current M6 or release-stage mechanism applies.
The earlier stats capture, stats-off bench, region output and raw counter/profile files are retained in the same scratch directory.
